content: The text provided appears to be a long list of references from various studies, trials, and publications related to nutrition, malnutrition, complementary feeding, micronutrient supplementation, and related topics. 1. Trials were conducted to optimize microbiota-directed complementary food prototypes for their ability to repair microbiota immaturity and assess their organoleptic acceptability. (2021) 2. Complementary food supplements were evaluated for their effectiveness in reducing childhood undernutrition. (2014) 3. A study investigated the effects of fortified complementary foods on vitamin A status and body pool size in Ghanaian infants. (2010) 4. Research in Kenya assessed the safety and efficacy of iron supplementation in children. (2014) 5. An evaluation of the Alive & Thrive program in Burkina Faso was conducted to assess its impact on child nutrition. (2017) 6. A trial was performed to evaluate the safety and tolerability of a novel medical food designed for managing iron deficiency anemia. (2015) 7. A study in Finland examined the use of fortified spreads as food supplements to alleviate malnutrition in underweight infants. (Date not specified) 8. A program in Mexico utilized mHealth technology to prevent childhood obesity. (2020) 9. Targeted zinc fortification programs were studied for their impact on plasma zinc concentrations. (2009) 10. Zinc and iron bioavailability from biofortified pearl millet was analyzed in a study involving international collaboration. (2012) 11. The iron status of breastfed infants was evaluated under two different iron supplementation regimens. (2005) 12. Cereal-based complementary foods were assessed as a source of iron for breastfed infants. (2006) 13. A randomized placebo-controlled trial in Guatemala investigated the effects of maize fortified with zinc. (2004) 14. The effectiveness of nutritional products in treating moderate acute malnutrition was evaluated in a clinical trial. (2013) 15. A comparison of two ready-to-use supplementary foods with differing protein quality was conducted for the treatment of moderate acute malnutrition. (2018) 16. The use of iron-fortified wheat flour to reduce anemia among estate populations in Sri Lanka was studied. (2004) 17. A study on baby iron bioavailability was conducted in collaboration with the University of Malawi. (2019) 18. Nutritional interventions were evaluated for their effects on metabolic responses in infants. (2021) 19. Nutritional supplementation in children aged 1-3 years with growth concerns was studied. (2021) 20. The relationship between infant nutrition and brain development was explored in a study. (2022) 21. A fortified food was compared to micronutrient supplements for distribution in a Mexican social protection program, based on a cluster-randomized trial and cost analysis. (2019) 22. A complementary food supplement was tested for its effects on growth and morbidity in Ghanaian infants. (2015) 23. The introduction of baby cereals and other complementary foods in the diets of infants and toddlers was analyzed for its impact on nutrient intake. (2020) 24. A cluster-randomized trial in Burkina Faso evaluated the effectiveness of treating moderate acute malnutrition in first-line health services. (2014) 25. The adequacy of nutrient intakes in severely and acutely malnourished children treated with different doses of ready-to-use therapeutic food was assessed. (2021) 26. A randomized controlled trial in South Africa compared the efficacy of complementary food products on child growth. (2016) 27. The effect of probiotic yogurt on salivary cariogenic microflora in children was studied in Iran. (2015) 28. The impact of complementary food containing small amounts of freshwater fish on whole blood n-3 fatty acids in Cambodian infants was evaluated. (2018) 29. The growth patterns of infants fed a mixture of extruded malted maize and cowpea were studied. (2003) 30. The effect of micronutrient-fortified complementary food on micronutrient status, growth, and development of disadvantaged urban South African infants was analyzed. (2003) 31. The effect of legume supplementation on the gut microbiota of rural Malawian infants was studied. (2020) 32. The efficacy of processed amaranth on anemia prevalence and hemoglobin levels in preschool children in South Ethiopia was evaluated. (2019) 33. Zinc supplementation between 1 and 6 months of life was studied for its effects on growth and morbidity in Bangladeshi infants. (2002) 34. The impact of an improved local ingredient-based complementary food fortified with iron and selected micronutrients on hemoglobin concentration was assessed. (2010) 35. Fortified complementary foods with or without alpha-amylase treatment were studied for their effects on hemoglobin levels and breast milk intake in Zambian infants. (2007) 36. Breast milk intake of rural infants given ready-to-use complementary food in South Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo, was evaluated. (2011) 37. The breast milk intake of Zambian infants given fortified complementary foods was studied. (2013) 38. Data from Kenya and Cambodia on the WinFood project highlighted constraints on field procedures. (2015) 39. A trial in Thika District developed and utilized amaranth-sorghum grain products to enhance the nutritional status of moderately malnourished children. (2016) 40. A strategy combining responsive feeding promotion with fortified cereal-based blends was tested to reduce anemia, micronutrient deficiencies, and stunting in infants in Madagascar. (2019) 41. The impact of biofortified maize consumption on serum carotenoid concentrations in Zambian children was studied. (2018) 42. Supplemental feeding with ready-to-use therapeutic food in Malawian children at risk of malnutrition was evaluated. (2005) 43. The acceptability of fortified, processed complementary foods by mothers and children in Tanzania was assessed. (2007) 44. A six-month intervention with two types of micronutrient-fortified complementary foods had distinct effects on growth in Vietnamese infants. (2012) 45. Complementary feeding with fortified spread and its association with severe stunting in rural Malawian children was studied. (2008) 46. Post-intervention growth of Malawian children who received dietary supplementation with lipid-based nutrient supplements or maize-soy flour was analyzed. (2009) 47. Supplementary feeding with fortified spread among moderately underweight rural Malawian children was evaluated. (2009) 48. The influence of feeding regimens on iron status during infancy was studied. (1980) 49. Developmental trajectories of poorly nourished toddlers receiving micronutrient supplements with and without energy were analyzed. (2002) 50. Supplementary feeding with locally-produced ready-to-use food for mildly wasted children in Indonesia was compared between daily and weekly programs. (2012) 51. Iron solubility and bioavailability in processed and unprocessed complementary food for Tanzanian infants were assessed using in vitro digestion and Caco-2 cell culture methods. (2006) 52. The effects of complementary feeding on the microbiome and oxidative stress in Canadian infants were studied in a randomized controlled trial. (2017) 53. The intake of energy-dense porridge liquefied by amylase of germinated wheat was evaluated in severely malnourished children recovering from diarrhea. (1994) 54. Macronutrient absorption and nitrogen balance in children with dysentery fed an amylase-treated energy-dense porridge were studied. (1997) 55. Nutrient absorption from an energy-dense diet liquefied with amylase from germinated wheat in infants with acute diarrhea was analyzed. (1997) 56. The impact of a nutritional support program on food diversity and consumption of iron-rich or iron-fortified foods in Mexican children was evaluated. (2013) 57. A food transfer program without formal education modified complementary feeding practices in poor rural Mexican communities. (2016) 58. Acceptability trials with ready-to-eat foods in rural areas were conducted. (1992) 59. The effect of supplementary feeding on recovery from mild to moderate wasting in preschool children was studied. (1991) 60. The effect of supplementary feeding on the prevention of mild-to-moderate wasting in conditions of endemic malnutrition in Guatemala was evaluated. (2002) 61. A pilot randomized controlled trial of a new supplementary food designed to enhance cognitive performance during malnutrition prevention and treatment was conducted. (2017) 62. The effects of food supplementation on cognitive function, cerebral blood flow, and nutritional status in young children at risk of undernutrition were studied. (2020) 63. A comparison of two ready-to-use supplementary foods with differing protein quality for the treatment of moderate acute malnutrition in Malawi was conducted. (2020) 64. The efficacy of different strategies to treat anemia in children was evaluated in a randomized clinical trial. (2010) 65. The impact of zinc supplementation on morbidity from diarrhea and respiratory infections among rural Guatemalan children was studied. (1997) 66. The role of iron and zinc supplementation in addressing growth retardation and iron deficiency anemia in Egyptian children was analyzed. (2003) 67. Barriers and enablers for scaling up a community-based grain bank intervention for improved infant and young child feeding in Ethiopia were explored. (2018) 68. The effect of biscuits fortified with haem iron on the intellectual status of preschool children was studied.
